challenges.title: Working Time Regulations, rest periods and data protection

items.title: Keeping the 48-hour week & opt-out under control
items.text: The Working Time Regulations 1998 cap average weekly working time at 48 hours, calculated over a standard 17-week reference period — extendable by agreement. Staff can opt out in writing, which makes manual tracking even harder.

items.title: Guaranteeing daily & weekly rest periods
items.text: The WTR require at least 11 consecutive hours of rest per 24 hours and 24 uninterrupted hours per 7-day period (Reg. 10 & 11) — error-prone to track by hand across rotating shifts.

items.title: Biometric time tracking as a data protection risk
items.text: In February 2024, the ICO took enforcement action against Serco Leisure after facial recognition and fingerprint clocking systems at 38 sites processed data on over 2,000 employees without a lawful basis — a warning sign for any time-tracking solution.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off UK businesses
solutions.subtitle: From automatic rest-period control to data-protection-compliant time tracking — everything works together.

items.title: 48-hour limit & opt-out managed automatically
items.text: Klacks continuously calculates the 17-week average under WTR Reg. 4 and flags anyone working beyond the 48-hour limit under an opt-out — fully traceable for any inspection.

items.title: Rest periods observed automatically
items.text: The 11-hour daily rest and 24-hour weekly rest under WTR Reg. 10 & 11 are factored into every shift plan automatically — breaches never occur in the first place.

items.title: Time tracking without the biometric risk
items.text: Klacks records working time without needing facial recognition or fingerprints — no Serco-Leisure-style case, no questions from the ICO.

items.title: On-premise: full data sovereignty
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure, and you choose the AI model yourself — in line with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, with no cross-border transfer of staff data at all.

items.title: Ready for the Employment Rights Act 2025
items.text: The Employment Rights Act 2025 received Royal Assent on 18 December 2025 and will in future govern advance notice periods for shifts and compensation for cancelled shifts — the exact thresholds have yet to be set. Klacks can easily be extended with new notice-period and compensation rules once they are confirmed.

items.title: Klacksy: rule-based, not a black box
items.text: The built-in AI assistant Klacksy schedules via voice or chat command — traceable through defined skills and rules, not an opaque AI decision.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: the assistant built into your team
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn't a bolted-on marketing chatbot — it's embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers use chat to check shift times, request swaps, or clarify availability. A built-in skills and rules system ensures Klacksy always makes traceable suggestions — never a black-box decision. For businesses with strict data protection requirements, the AI model can also be hosted locally.

example.title: The 48-hour week and rest periods, at a glance
example.text: Klacks automatically detects when an employee is approaching the 48-hour limit or a rest period under WTR Reg. 10 would fall short, and suggests the adjustment straight away — no manual recalculating required.
